intent: Hold the best-supported geometry fixed at the iteration 5 values (±0.036 m outer pair, 15 mm spacing, y=0.04, 0.016 footprint, 0.18 m by 0.12 m body, 0.8 kg, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheel radius). The race then measures the controller, not the geometry. Expected: a score near 52.4, with slalom line_loss_events still 1 unless the Integrator's gain or speed change clears it.
learning: Geometry is now at a plateau: sensor footprint, outer spread and body are each neutral or confirmed, and the body change at 0.14 m and 0.6 kg cost about 6 points. The slalom line loss of 1 persists at ±0.036, so the next gain is most likely in controller speed or gain. Ask the Integrator whether kp, kd or base_speed changes clear the slalom line loss, and whether the outer sensors saturate at the 0.036 reach. If the Integrator reports that the line loss clears, the sensing layout is sufficient. If it does not, the remaining untested geometry lever is wheel_track (turn rate per wheel differential), which I would test next with a single-variable change.
rationale: Iteration 5 raced at ±0.036 m outer sensors, 0.016 footprint, baseline body, and scored 52.356, a small gain over iteration 4 (52.198). The gain is mostly on the s-bend (progress 0.1575, rms 0.0284). The slalom did not improve: line_loss_events stayed at 1.0 on every track, progress fell from 0.112 to 0.109, rms rose from 0.0302 to 0.0303, and oscillation rose from 0.156 to 0.159. The Integrator's rule for this case is that line loss staying at 1 with progress near 0.11 even at ±0.036 means the geometry is no longer the binding constraint, and the controller's speed or gain is the likely limit. The rms stayed below the 0.032 threshold, so the outer sensors do not need to return to ±0.03. Across the last four races, every geometry change has moved the score by less than about 0.2 except the body change, which cost 6 points. The base body (0.18 m, 0.8 kg), footprint (0.016) and outer spread (±0.036) are now the best-supported set, so I hold them fixed. Changing the body again or the row position is not supported by the evidence, and I have no sensing hypothesis that predicts a meaningful gain. I therefore keep the geometry identical to iteration 5. This race acts as a replicate on the geometry side, and it lets the Integrator's gain changes be read against a fixed platform. Wheel track, wheel radius, body width and mass are unchanged, so the result isolates the controller. I expect a score near 52.4, with slalom line loss at 1 unless the controller is retuned.
